headline: Gold Hits $4,580 as IRAN CEASEFIRE HOPE Lifts Precious Metals; Silver Holds at $76
snippet: Gold climbed for a second straight session to $4,580/oz after reports of a US-Iran preliminary peace agreement eased inflation and rate fears. Silver steadied at $76.43/oz (+0.51%) though both metals remain on track for a modest monthly decline as elevated interest rate expectations weigh.

headline: ERIC SPROTT Drops $25M Into Canada's First Natural Hydrogen Discovery
snippet: MAX Power Mining (CSE: MAXX) closed a $25M non-brokered private placement at $2.00/unit with legendary resource investor Eric Sprott to advance Lawson — Canada's first confirmed subsurface natural hydrogen system, validated by three independent labs in Saskatchewan. Sprott now controls ~19% of the company on a non-diluted basis, with $40M+ in treasury to fund aggressive drilling across the Lawson Complex and broader Saskatchewan land package.

headline: GROUP ELEVEN BALLYWIRE: 62.5m of 5.6% Zn-Pb + COPPER-SILVER ZONES Confirmed in Step-Out
snippet: Group Eleven Resources (TSXV: ZNG) announced three new drill holes at Ballywire, Ireland on May 28, including 62.5m of 5.6% Zn+Pb with 25 g/t Ag, plus a 720m step-out that cut four copper-silver zones up to 6.8m at 0.10% Cu. The Glencore-backed project has four rigs turning on a C$12M-funded 67,000–75,000m drill program.

headline: ACID SHOCK: China's Sulfuric Export Ban Crushes Copper Smelters; COMEX Nears Record $6.40/lb
snippet: China's May–December suspension of sulfuric acid exports removes ~3 million tonnes from global markets, hitting Chile hardest where Chinese acid supplied 37% of imports. Wood Mackenzie states the binding constraint on copper output is now 'acid, refining charges, and trade policy — not geology.' COMEX copper held near a record $6.40/lb supported by AI data center demand and clean energy grid buildout.

headline: GR SILVER'S BEST-EVER HOLE: 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag at San Marcial — System Still Growing
snippet: GR Silver Mining (TSXV: GRSL) reported hole SMS26-04 at San Marcial, Mexico: 45.1m at 1,623 g/t Ag, including 8.25m at 8,579 g/t Ag — the highest-grade intercept in project history. The result confirms continuity of high-grade silver mineralization along key structural features; a 20,000m step-out drill program is ongoing with an updated resource estimate and PEA targeted for H2 2026.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING Finds 71m Surface Oxide Au-Ag Zone at Northern Apollo — HEAP LEACH Possible
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) outlined a new outcropping oxide gold-silver zone in the northern portion of Apollo, Colombia: 71.2m at 1.95 g/t AuEq (0.75 g/t Au + 87 g/t Ag) from surface. A 700m x 200m corridor of oxidized mineralization has been traced; metallurgical test work is underway to evaluate potential heap-leach economics ahead of a maiden NI 43-101 resource estimate expected mid-2027.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT DEFICIT: 215 MILLION OUNCES in 2026 — Biggest Shortfall on Record
snippet: The Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects a 215 million ounce supply deficit — the largest on record and the sixth consecutive annual shortfall. Total silver supply rises just 1.5% to a decade-high 1.05 billion oz while industrial and investment demand continue to outpace mine output; cumulative deficit since 2021 now stands at 762 million ounces.

headline: ARCELORMITTAL CANADA Ordered to Pay RECORD $100M Fisheries Act Fine for Quebec Mine Pollution
snippet: A Quebec court handed ArcelorMittal Exploitation Minière Canada a $100M fine — the largest penalty ever under Canada's Fisheries Act — after the company pleaded guilty to 100 counts of discharging nickel and zinc into fish-bearing waters between 2014 and 2022 at its Mont-Wright and Fire Lake iron ore mines. The court also ordered a $250K investigation cost reimbursement and a full environmental remediation plan by February 2027.

headline: NdPr RARE EARTHS Up 88% YTD Despite April Selloff; CHINA QUOTA DECISION Looms in June
snippet: NdPr oxide fell 21% in April to ~$100/kg after a 105% run from January's open near $53/kg, but the correction reflects profit-taking rather than a structural reversal — NdPr remains up 88% year-to-date. The critical catalyst to watch is China's mid-year MIIT mining quota announcement, typically released in June, which will indicate whether supply constraints tighten or ease in H2 2026.

headline: USA RARE EARTH (USAR) Is Crushing the Market in 2026 — But Can It Deliver the Mine-to-Magnet Dream?
snippet: USA Rare Earth (NYSE: USAR), owner of the Texas Round Top polymetallic deposit and an Oklahoma permanent magnet factory, has been one of 2026's sharpest outperformers as critical minerals geopolitics drive the stock. Motley Fool examines whether the mine-to-magnet vertical integration thesis has genuine millionaire-maker potential — or is pricing in flawless execution the company hasn't yet demonstrated.

headline: NEWMONT vs SSR MINING: Which Gold Major Offers Better Torque as Gold Approaches $4,600?
snippet: Motley Fool puts Newmont (NYSE: NEM) head-to-head with SSR Mining (TSX: SSRM) as gold hovers near $4,600/oz, comparing balance sheet strength, all-in sustaining costs, production growth, and margin expansion. With gold miners broadly lagging the metal's YTD gains, analysts argue select producers are still trading at depressed multiples despite expanding free cash flow.

headline: AI DATA CENTER BOOM Set to TURBOCHARGE URANIUM DEMAND — Utilities Re-Enter Market Above $100/lb
snippet: A global investor survey by Uranium.io finds the rapid buildout of AI hyperscale data centers is reshaping long-term nuclear generation expectations and driving utilities back to the contracting market after years of under-procurement. Uranium spot prices have moved back above $100/lb as the investment case tightens; Denison Mines recently received final CNSC regulatory approval for its Wheeler River Phoenix ISR project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin.
